stem: You see a 4-year-old boy who is extremely active and meets the diagnostic criteria for ADHD. His mother is highly stressed. Which ONE of the following management strategies is most appropriate at this stage?

options.text: Behaviour management focusing on parent training
Just monitor his progress because he may improve as he matures
Trial him on stimulant medication before he starts school

explanation: For a preschool-aged child with ADHD, first-line management is behavioural intervention with parent training and support. Medication is usually reserved for more severe cases or when behavioural strategies are insufficient, and monitoring alone is not appropriate when there is significant impairment and family stress.
rationale: Preschool ADHD is managed initially with behavioural strategies and parent training; medication is not first-line.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Parent-focused behaviour management is the preferred initial treatment in preschool-aged children with ADHD.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. Although some children improve with time, active management is indicated when symptoms are causing impairment.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. Preschool attendance may help with routine and socialisation, but it is not the primary treatment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. Stimulants are not first-line in most 4-year-olds and are generally considered after behavioural therapy.
